STREAM 01 (88 sources, 29 findings, 34 numbered implications) - Existing Harnesses. Load-bearing results: (1) INSTRUCTION FILES ARE AN ATTACK SURFACE, not documentation - CSA research note confirms indirect prompt injection via AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules across ALL major harnesses (Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Roo Code, Cline, Junie, Zed); ReadSecBench ~84% ASR from README-embedded commands, ~91% two links removed, 93% of 15 human reviewers MISSED it; AIShellJack 41-84%, Cursor in auto-approval mode 83.4%; NVIDIA AI Red Team got Codex to hide a 5-min sleep delay from PR summaries via a build-time-written AGENTS.md; Prompt Security got Copilot to exfiltrate creds from a cloned repo; TrojanForge sustains >60% poisoning with >90% backdoor injection across 4 harnesses x 12 models. NO existing harness defends against this. (2) THE HEAD-TO-HEAD HOOK EVALUATION (zhuyansen/awesome-claude-code-hooks, 12 hooks x 12 actions, 2026-10-10) is the single most decision-relevant measurement found anywhere: with prompts skipped 6 of 12 hooks stopped NONE of 8 risky actions; with NO hook at all Claude Code's own prompts stopped 7/8 risky AND wrongly stopped 3/4 ORDINARY actions; the best hook (nomos) scored 7/8 with 0/4 false positives. So: permission prompts are the load-bearing layer, the hook category is much weaker than its marketing, and FALSE POSITIVES ON ORDINARY WORK are the mechanism that drives beginners to --dangerously-skip-permissions. (3) FACTORY DROID SHIPS A NAMED AUTONOMY DIAL (Off/Low/Medium/High risk bands, orthogonal to Spec/Normal/Mission mode, plus a blocklist that survives --skip-permissions-unsafe, and program-resolution before matching so bash -c wrappers cannot slip through) and ANTIGRAVITY 2.0 HAS A PRESET LITERALLY NAMED 'Turbo' that disables the sandbox and grants full filesystem - so vibe-fence's dial is a PORT+rename of shipped patterns, not a greenfield invention, and 'turbo' is a dangerous name to ship. (4) HARNESS IS A MEASURED VARIABLE: The Scaffold Effect (arXiv:2607.22585) shows up to 40x tokens-per-solved-task spread across harnesses with 0-8pp pass-rate spread and model-independent failure fingerprints; arXiv:2609.20804 shows rule-based elision before LLM summarization wins and that making elided content recoverable adds machinery models never use with NO accuracy gain, and that planning is a COST saver for strong models not an accuracy lever; arXiv:2607.03691 (TOSEM) finds NO significant SWE-bench improvement across 35 Qwen Code releases with the LLM fixed, with later versions burning ~2x tokens - so vibe-fence's value must be deterministic logic, not just instruction files. (5) OUTCOMES: arXiv:2606.23130 audits 200 deployed vibe-coded apps -> 91.0% have >=1 vulnerability, 65.77% Critical/High, traced to 8 failure modes under 3 defect classes (memory/objective/knowledge), and says harness improvements REDUCE BUT DO NOT ELIMINATE risk; arXiv:2604.12311 finds ~45% silent-failure rate among executed scripts and that LESS FORMAL PROMPTS increase hallucinated safety variables. (6) THE TEACHING DIAL HAS PRECEDENT: the Explanation Gate study (arXiv:2602.20206) cut epistemic debt 69.3->27.6 (-41.7 points) for only 14.2 min cost, and a Conceptual Inquiry stance (explanatory questions only) scored 65-86% while matching full-delegation speed - so interactional stance, not tool access, determines learning. DIVERGES from both sibling files on 8 counts (documented in the 'Contradictions with sibling reports' section): (a) the dial is NOT a greenfield invention - Factory and Antigravity ship one; (b) 'no harness enforces safety structurally' is overstated - AGENT-HOOKS-0.1 defines a fail-closed deny contract with a Conformance Test Kit, the Standard Agent Spec requires fail-closed composition, and DCG blocks across 15+ agents; the real gap is the BUNDLE plus AUDITABILITY, not the primitives; (c) instruction files are an active execution surface with measured ASR, not passive advice; (d) Antigravity's permission algebra is more expressive than Windsurf Cascade's Todo list; (e) Aider's auto-git is recovery not prevention and should not be the headline; (f) Cline's 'Safe Commands' asks the model to police itself (CVE-2026-52025) and its Approve/Deny dialog does not gate the URL-preview click (CVE-2026-52024) - a safety filter that delegates its verdict to the constrained model is not a filter; (g) harness quality regresses silently across releases, so a file-only vibe-fence will rot like the incumbents; (h) Archestra is strong but operationally impossible for a solo vibe-coder - the file-based stack won the measured criterion. COVERS 40+ harness families including several ABSENT from all sibling files: AGENT-HOOKS-0.1 + Standard Agent Specification + Microsoft Agent Framework hooks, Agent Client Protocol (ACP, ~40 agents), Factory Droid autonomy levels, Antigravity 2.0 permissions, destructive_command_guard, agentlint, claude-code-hooks, nomos, ClawSentry, Task Master, Vibe Kanban (now sunsetting), Codex Security, Kiro specs/steering/checkpoints, Warp rules, Amazon Q, Kimi Code CLI, Qwen Code, Crush, OpenHands skills taxonomy, Replit/Lovable/Bolt, skills.sh, the teach skill, Hallmark, and the VibeIncidents live log (60 incidents, 318 sources). KEY GAPS: documentation survey only, no hands-on installation; Kiro hooks/checkpoints and Qwen Code approval-mode pages could not be extracted beyond navigation; ACP safety surface is absence-of-evidence on one page, not verified absence; no consumer-builder security audits. STREAMS 02-06 also completed. Stream 03 (48 sources, 35 findings, 19 numbered implications) and stream 05 (35 sources, 22 findings). For stream 03, the load-bearing results are: Huang et al. 2024 (arXiv:2310.01798) as the key NEGATIVE result - unaided self-critique DEGRADES reasoning (Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0->36.5), plus their cost-matched Table 7 showing multi-agent debate LOSES to plain majority voting (83.0% vs 88.2% at 9 responses); Huang et al. also refute Reflexion's headline as a cross-model comparison (91% vs GPT-4's 80%, not a same-model ablation); Brown et al. 2024 (arXiv:2407.21787) for SWE-bench Lite 15.9%->56% at 250 samples AND the verifier-flakiness caveat (11.3% of test suites flaky, 35/122 CodeContests false negatives) that NEITHER sibling file mentions; Wang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2504.14047) for the reasoning-model-era REVERSAL - simple majority voting beats MoA/best-of-N/sequential revision, plus the 'reasoning floor' non-reasoning models cannot escape; Chen et al. 2023 (arXiv:2307.10397) CodeT 65.8% HumanEval +18.8pp absolute; Chen et al. 2023 (arXiv:2311.17311) USC as a fallback selector that MATCHES but does not beat execution (BIRD-SQL 42.4->45.5, not the +10-15pp the muse-spark file claims); R2E-Gym (arXiv:2504.07164) for <20% test distinguishability; Gao/Schulman/Hilton 2022 for reward-model over-optimization making judge-gated BoN actively harmful; 'Efficient Agents' (arXiv:2508.02694) and OAgents (arXiv:2506.15741) for the cost-of-pass metric and the Pass@1-vs-Pass@3 inflation trap; FrugalGPT (arXiv:2305.05176) 98% cost reduction and early-abstention cascades (arXiv:2502.09054) for weak-model routing; arXiv:2512.10218 for SWE-bench Verified being partly a memory benchmark. DIVERGES from both sibling files: (a) ranks multi-agent debate as DOMINATED at equal cost, not merely expensive; (b) argues the harness's quality must come from the VERIFIER, not the architecture, inverting the 'richer elicitation' thesis on modern models; (c) flags the Reflexion 67%->91% misattribution in google-gemini-3.8-flash; (d) adds the 2026 vibe-coding literature (arXiv:2511.00202, 2609.38606, 2507.22614, 2605.07751, 2512.24939) including the 'interface flattening' accountability-surface framing; (e) proposes a model-tier switch in the harness config given the reasoning floor. Stream 05 remains as previously reported: the dial is a fixed schema + cognitive forcing, not a verbosity ladder, and turbo is a per-action-class friction ladder, not a boolean. NOTES for stream 05: kept in this manifest's streams_completed so a synthesis agent sees both runs for this model; the stream-05 file itself was written first and is unchanged by this pass. FLAG for synthesis: whether Muse Spark is reasoning-optimized is an OPEN QUESTION that determines the elicitation design (parallel sample+vote vs re-sample-with-execution), and it should be settled before locking the harness architecture. STREAM 02 (harness -> output quality): 46 sources, 18 findings, 29 numbered implications. Load-bearing: Gloaguen et al. 2026 (arXiv:2602.11988) - the first rigorous benchmark of AGENTS.md: LLM-generated context files REDUCE task success (-3% avg, drops in 5 of 8 settings) and cost +20-23%, developer-written files buy only +4%, and 'map not manual' overviews do NOT accelerate file discovery (100% of Sonnet-4.5 files had an overview; no reduction in steps-to-relevant-file). The folklore comes from undocumented repos: strip all docs and generated files then help (+2.7%) and beat developer docs. Liu 2026 (arXiv:2605.05716) full-factorial CCI: the all-in 5-component scaffold is beaten by a proper subset in EVERY condition (32% HotpotQA/8B, 79% GSM8K); Planning has a NEGATIVE Shapley value; 90% of 183 submodularity violations sign-flip so greedy add-one-at-a-time selection is unreliable; Tool Use captures 70% of scaffold value. RAG-MCP (arXiv:2505.03275): tool-selection accuracy 13.62% -> 43.13% with retrieval over tool schemas, >50% prompt-token cut. Anthropic code-execution-with-MCP: 150,000 -> 2,000 tokens (-98.7%). AIShellJack (arXiv:2509.22040) 41-84% attack success across Cursor/Copilot x Claude-4/Gemini-2.5-Pro (Cursor auto-approve 83.4%); ReadSecBench (arXiv:2603.11862) exfiltration up to 85%, 0% human detection across 15 participants, no rule-based or LLM-based defense reliable without unacceptable false positives; OWASP AST01 Malicious Skills (3 lines of SKILL.md markdown exfiltrates SSH keys; 5 of top-7 ClawHub skills at peak infection were malware; 73.2% of malicious skills hide shadow features); NVIDIA Red Team - a malicious Go dependency writes AGENTS.md at build time (CODEX_PROXY_CERT detection) and instructs Codex to inject a 5-minute sleep and conceal it from PR summaries. ClawSentry (arXiv:2608.21101): the measured defense (contextual ASR 39.55% -> 2.61%, task success held within 0.73pp) AND the measured failure of the obvious defense (Safety Skill + AGENTS.md: 25/60 -> 18/60 with task success FALLING 20/60 -> 15/60; Claude Guardrails Full 19/60 -> 20/60 = no better than nothing). SkillSafetyBench (arXiv:2605.12015): 42.1% full-pass-conditional ASR - attacks succeed while the task still passes, so task success alone is an unsafe release gate. ClawsBench (arXiv:2604.05172): full scaffolding worth +39 to +63pp of capability but unsafe-action rates 7-33%, and capability does NOT correlate with safety (Claude Opus had the highest success AND a tied-highest unsafe rate). How Fast Do Agents Rot (arXiv:2609.01660, n=10,664): every model incl. deployed systems collapses from near-perfect to near-zero within 16 steps; degradation is driven by STEP COUNT not context length (logit slope -0.69 vs -0.44, p=3e-6) and bounding the window steepens decay - contradicting a lost-in-the-middle explanation. RULER (arXiv:2404.06654): only half of 32K-claiming models hold up at 32K. NoLiMa (arXiv:2502.05167): 10 of 12 models drop below 50% of baseline at 32K once literal-match crutches are removed. General AgentBench (arXiv:2602.18998): context ceiling in sequential scaling and a verification gap in parallel scaling, so neither test-time-scaling method helps in practice. mini-swe-agent (github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent): ~100 lines, NO tools other than bash, >74% SWE-bench Verified - the same lab that built the 2024 ACI now says most of it is no longer needed. Cursor harness blogs: 66% system-prompt trim by replacing 'DO NOT' lists with positive definitions; ARC-AGI-3 13.3% -> 38.3% on the SAME model via harness alone; per-model tool formatting; a BIGGER SUMMARIZER MODEL MEASURED AS NEGLIGIBLE. Archestra: weak models expose harness bugs strong models hide; open model ~90% of tasks at <$1/run vs $20-30/run for frontier; one model swung 58-88% across a week. OpenAI (arXiv openai.com/index/separating-signal-from-noise): ~30% of SWE-bench Pro tasks are broken; their prior recommendation retracted. DIVERGES from siblings: contradicts muse-spark's 'map not manual' as `practiced` (it was measured, and static overviews do not work); contradicts gemini-3.8-flash's universal filtered-ACI recommendation (now model-tier-conditional, not universal); downgrades Architect/Editor from `proven` to `practiced` (vendor benchmark, architect stage not isolated); grounds the pink-elephant claim in a measured Cursor trim rather than folklore; and argues the PRIMARY driver of negative-constraint failure is instruction COUNT (Curse of Instructions, P(all)~P(one)^n), not negative framing per se. ADDS the safety angle nobody else covered: vibe-fence's own mechanism (injecting files the agent reads as instructions) IS the measured attack vector, so the fence needs file-integrity checks, an untrusted-data channel, pre-execution skill admission control, and an adversarial fence bench - and if it cannot measurably reduce the 41-85% injection rate it is increasing risk while claiming to reduce it. FLAG for synthesis: vibe-fence's flagship deliverable is a generated AGENTS.md, and the best available evidence says a generated AGENTS.md is a NET NEGATIVE on well-documented repos. This should be settled before the fence's positioning is locked. STREAM 04 (69 sources, 60 rules, 13 numbered implications) — the AI-specific layer that the other two contributors did not cover. Version facts verified, not assumed: OWASP Top 10 is 2025, not 2021 (A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures replaced A06:2021; SSRF folded into A01:2025; A10:2025 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions is new); the OWASP LLM list is now GenAI LLM Top 10 2026 (published 2026-08-03), and there are separate OWASP projects for MCP Top 10, Agentic Skills Top 10, and Agentic Applications 2026. 11 rules (A-01..A-10) treat the AGENT as the attack surface: secrets never in prompts/config, repo content is untrusted, security controls enforced OUTSIDE the LLM, least-agency + agent identity, MCP server pinning, LLM output as untrusted data, scoped read-only AI DB identity, bounded model consumption, PII redaction before model calls, and system prompt as guidance-not-boundary. Supply chain is a POLICY not a scan: npm ci + committed lockfile, pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies allowlist, minimum-release-age cooldown, and a slopsquat verification gate for AI-hallucinated package names. Every rule names an exact command, config key, or file, plus a Class tag: 48 fully deterministic (gate-able), 8 hybrid (deterministic gate + secondary judgement/teaching), 4 not deterministic (A-21 rotation procedure, A-40 issue-worthiness, A-43 build-time mental model, A-55 data-purpose legitimacy) so they can only ever be warn/nudge. Severity roll-up 24 block / 31 warn / 5 nudge; a cumulative app-profile escalation (local/shared/public) covers all 60 rules exactly once, and the 5 nudge rules never become block. Section 10 is the meta-guardrail: 10 named over-blocking patterns (secret-scanner false positives on public keys, CSP blocking on day one, PR requirements for solo hobby apps, etc.) — a guardrail a user can trivially disable is worthless. CONTRADICTS the siblings: google-gemini anchors to OWASP 2021 categories throughout; gemini has the right severity for the NEXT_PUBLIC_ leak but not the mechanism (Next.js inlines it into the browser bundle at build time, and Vercel's Secret type only makes the dashboard value write-only), muse-spark has neither. Agrees with both that destructive-git interception is a block while Conventional Commits stays a nudge. Deliberately shallow (defer to siblings): JWT/OAuth detail, RLS policies, file uploads, SSRF/outbound allowlisting, non-Vercel deploy targets, framework detection for VITE_/PUBLIC_ prefixes. STREAM 06 (Meta models for the hackathon) — 47 sources (45 primary Meta/Cerebral Valley/AI-at-Meta + 2 third-party), 38 findings, 15 contradiction rows vs the sibling files, 21 numbered implications with P0-P3 priorities. Load-bearing results, all from live dev.meta.ai docs fetched 2026-10-20 (the .md variants serve clean markdown; Exa's keyless backend 429'd repeatedly so I used terminal curl on the same canonical URLs): (1) THERE ARE SIX MODEL LINES, NOT FOUR. dev.meta.ai/docs/models lists Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, Muse Image, Muse Voice Transcribe, SAM 3.1, Muse Glimmer, plus Muse Spark Open. NEITHER SIBLING FILE MENTIONS MUSE WONDER, which is 'Meta's most capable model, built for complex software engineering and long-horizon agentic work' at $4.00/$20.00 per 1M (Standard only on Model API; Muse Wonder Full is Muse Code-subscription-only at $50/$200 per month). Meta's own coding-agent and agent-framework guides use muse-wonder-1.0 for the main loop and muse-spark-1.3 for subagents, and Spark and Wonder 'take the same requests on the same endpoints, so moving a workload between them is a model ID change' -> the whole routing policy is a one-line model swap. RECOMMENDATION: Wonder for the plan-and-verify gate, Spark 1.3 for classification/teaching/triage, Glimmer 30B local for high-volume secret/severity classification. (2) MUSE CODE READS AGENTS.md. 'From your workspace root, Muse Code walks up to the nearest .git boundary. At each directory level, it checks AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, then .claude/CLAUDE.md; the first existing file in that order wins.' Project rules beat user rules; deeper files beat shallower; project rules load only after workspace trust. So vibe-fence's core file format is ALREADY a first-class Muse Code contract and the 'Muse Code adapter' reduces to writing files, not building a plugin. Meta also states the injection rule to copy: project MEMORY.md is read even in an untrusted workspace while skills/rules/hooks are trust-gated, so 'treat a repo's MEMORY.md as a prompt-injection surface'. (3) CONTRIBUTOR MODE IS A DATA DEAL, NOT JUST A DISCOUNT. $0.10/$0.20 per 1M vs $1.25/$4.25, but 'your content may be used to train future Meta models' where content = 'the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back'. For a product whose pitch is code safety, shipping user source into a training set by default contradicts the thesis. Also 150 RPM vs 3,000 RPM, and no Contributor mode for Muse Wonder. (4) THE RESPONSES API'S RECOMMENDED MODE IS STATELESS, NOT previous_response_id — both siblings say the opposite. 'Stateless encrypted reasoning replay (recommended): resend the conversation each turn... Nothing is stored server-side' vs server-managed history via previous_response_id as the alternative. The Responses API is the only endpoint that carries chain of thought across turns. (5) THREE DOCUMENTED CONSTRAINTS THAT WILL BREAK AN IMPLEMENTATION: recursive JSON Schemas -> HTTP 400 (so the issue->solution->plan queue MUST be flattened); tool_search + text.format on one request -> HTTP 400 (so run tool search on an earlier turn); reasoning_effort 'none' -> HTTP 400 on both Wonder and Spark (so 'silent' mode must mean 'do not call the model', not 'none'). (6) tool_search IS THE TOKEN-COST LEVER: deferred tool schemas keep name+description visible, load on demand, append at the end of context to preserve the cache prefix, group into namespaces of <10 functions, Responses-only. Combined with 'no long-context premium' and prompt caching, a 1M-context harness is affordable. (7) SAM 3.1 IS A POOR FIT AND I SAY SO: 'One concept per request: there is no multi-concept syntax. Comma, semicolon, and plus lists return zero matches', boxes+masks only with NO semantic labels, endpoint is POST /v1/responses with model sam-3.1 (not /v1/cv/sam-3.1/segment as google-gemini claims), and the API's 16-object limit applies to PROMPTED objects, not multi-concept detection. The sibling's 'screenshot -> navbar/sidebar/hero_card -> Spark' mockup bridge is not implementable as written. MINIMAL CREDIBLE USE, stated honestly: click-to-teach UI auditing (user clicks -> box+point prompt -> pixel mask -> Spark reasons over the masked crop), framed as a TEACHING feature that does NOT improve code correctness, and only as an appendix beat, never in the critical path. Meta's own documented ordering is Spark-decides-the-concept THEN SAM-produces-the-mask, so any pipeline must not reverse it. (8) HONEST POSITIONING: Muse Code already has approval + OS sandbox (Seatbelt/bubblewrap), staged compound-command review, and read-only .git/.muse/.agents, so vibe-fence CANNOT claim 'we add approvals and sandboxing for Muse Code'. The defensible claim is portability across runtimes + the teaching/detection layer Meta does not provide. (9) OPEN WEIGHTS: Muse Spark Open is 816B/42B-active needing 8xB300 and ~2TB VRAM (NOT self-hostable by a hackathon team, contradicting the muse-spark sibling's framing); Muse Glimmer 30B dense is 17-20GB quantized, Apache-2.0, 128K context, with Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM/SGLang support, and Meta's Connect recap says it is 'designed to run on a single GPU or Mac Mini'. Glimmer is the on-device path and the waiver names Glimmer explicitly. (10) RUBRIC FROM THE WAIVER, NOT A BLOG: Impact 30% / Use of Meta AI Tooling 25% / Demo 25% / Technical Depth and Execution 20%; waiver names 'Muse Spark, Glimmer, SAM 3, and any other Meta AI products identified on the Event page'. Prize split Indie $400k (1st $150k) vs Startup $550k (1st $250k). (11) WINNING PATTERNS FROM META'S OWN PRIOR HACKATHON: the 2025 LlamaCon Hackathon (238 devs, 44 submissions, $35k) winners were OrgLens (expert matching from Jira/GitHub/docs), Compliance Wizards (fraud detection), Llama CCTV Operator ('operators define events in simple language' - direct prior art for the teaching dial), and Best Llama API Usage Geo-ML (long context to turn a pile of documents into a structured artifact - the parallel for vibe-fence is a project health report, not a chat answer). (12) MISSED CAPABILITY: the `computer` tool (Responses API only, model supplies only the action protocol, you supply the environment) enables a 'fix this' bug-reproduction loop for non-technical users - a real 'beyond basic integration' beat, with the harness owning the safety. COULD NOT VERIFY: SAM throughput figures ('32fps on H100' appears on no official page - NOT repeated), Muse Image max output resolution (sibling's '1600px' unverified), the specific geo-blocked country list (policy table renders client-side; the Pakistan/Ethiopia/Venezuela/Iraq/Cambodia + Muse-Image-in-India list is third-party and flagged snippet-only), Muse Code /grill and /goal slash commands (/plan IS confirmed in the official interactive docs), the Muse Code TypeScript/MSP SDK, and the Muse Glimmer launch date. No live API call was made (no key available) so all API facts are documentation-derived, not execution-verified. STREAM 05 (revised 2026-10-20 after the other streams landed) - added U-04b after independently verifying the
"turbo" naming risk against primary vendor docs: Factory Droid ships a four-band Autonomy Level (off/low/medium/high)
with a blocklist that holds at every band; Google Antigravity 2.0 ships a preset literally named "Turbo" whose own
docs table reads sandbox=Disabled, terminal=Allowed (unrestricted), file access=Full filesystem. Decision: adopt
Factory's SHAPE, do not adopt the "Turbo" LABEL - a mode named for speed reads as the removal of a cost when what
actually changes is the guarantee, which is the same misreading that produces --dangerously-skip-permissions. The
turbo contract is now `fence mode [guarded|assisted|autonomous|open]`, named by guarantee, default `guarded`.
